call_points.text: Management reaffirmed its target to reach $2 billion in revenue by FY30.
Earlier ₹700 Cr capex for 50,000 engines expansion is coming online by April 2027.
Powergen unit sales grew 41% to over 50,000 units in FY26, outperforming industry growth of 18%.
R&D spend remains steady at 2% of revenue and 2% of capex.
Standalone net cash position including treasury investments stands at ₹552 Cr.
Domestic Powergen saw strong volume growth across LHP, MHP, and HHP higher than industry rates.
Marine segment witnessed its highest ever order booking in Q4 FY26.
Total debt at ₹5,042 Cr and treasury assets at ₹846 Cr as of March 31, 2026.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The ITD has made additions to the returned income of the Company for FY 2014-15 on account of capital subsidy received from Government of Maharashtra, disallowance of provision for warranty and few other expenses/ deductions during the scrutiny assessment order passed u/s 143(3) of the Income Tax Act, 1961. Quantum of claim is Rs. 26,84,25,463.
tax_litigation.status: The company has filed an appeal before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) (CIT(A)/ First Appellate Authority) and the same is currently pending. Based on the past precedents in Company's own case as well as other judicial pronouncements, the Company is of the view that the likelihood of these additions being deleted by the appellate authorities is high and there may not be any material claim against the Company which may have any impact on the company. There is no further development for Q3 of FY 2025-26.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The ITD had made additions to the returned income of the Company for FY 2022-23 on account of disallowance of provision for warranty during the scrutiny assessment order passed u/s 143(3) of the Income Tax Act, 1961. During the course of the scrutiny assessment the SCN was issued on 27th February 2025, proposing total disallowances having a tax impact of INR 19.17 Cr. tax_litigation.status: The company has filed an appeal before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) (CIT(A)/ First Appellate Authority) and the same is currently pending. Based on the past precedents in Company's own case as well as other judicial pronouncements, the Company is of the view that the likelihood of these additions being deleted by the courts of law is very high and there will not be any material claim against the Company which will have any impact on the Company. There is no further development for Q3 of FY 2025-26.

operating_notes.text: B2B segment now includes Farm Mechanization Solutions following reorganization from 1st April 2025.
Standalone quarterly sales reached a record ₹1,522 Cr in Q4FY26.
B2B business recorded full year and Q4 FY26 highest ever revenues.
Standalone B2C business transfer to KFD effective 11th October 2025 has no impact on consolidated financial results.
Existing engine capacity is appx. 1,35,000 engines p.a. with ~75% capacity utilization.
Received GST order for FY22-23 with tax demand of ₹5.90 Cr and penalty of ₹0.59 Cr.
Subsidiary KASPL received MCA approval for business commencement following ₹9 Cr capital infusion for defence and railways business.
KOEL sold over 50,000 genset units in FY26, capturing market share as industry grew 18% to 179,000 units.
Board approved ₹1,400 Cr capex over 2 years for 20,000 engines targeting HHP capacity at Kagal plant.
Gross international sales exceeded ₹1,000 Cr in FY26.
Standalone segment revenue in Q1FY27: power gen ₹720 Cr (+18%), industrial ₹368 Cr (+19%), distribution and aftermarket ₹268 Cr (+20%), international ₹106 Cr (-11%).
KOEL Fluid Dynamics revenue was broadly flat at ₹294 Cr with domestic sales up and exports down; Arka AUM stood at ₹7,651 Cr across about 136 branches.
Cash conversion cycle was 25 days with inventory days up slightly to 264.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹2,116.23 Cr, net profit ₹155.22 Cr (+22.6% YoY).
2026-05-14: Kirloskar Oil Engines reported Q4FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹2,116 Cr (+21% YoY) and PAT of ₹162 Cr (+47% YoY), alongside a total dividend of 350%.
Kirloskar Oil Engines uploaded its Q4 FY26 investor presentation highlighting 21% YoY consolidated net sales growth.
Kirloskar Oil Engines approved a ₹1,400 Cr capex at Kagal to expand engine capacity by 20,000 units p.a. over 2 years.
Kirloskar Oil Engines approved the incorporation of a wholly owned subsidiary in Amsterdam, Netherlands, with an investment of ₹2 Cr.
Farah Tehmton Irani and Farah Irani informed BSE and NSE of the Investors & Analysts Conference Call held on 14 May 2026 at 7:00 PM (IST) to discuss Q4 & FY26 audited results.
Rahul Kirloskar, promoter of Kirloskar Oil Engines Limited, declares no encumbrance on shares as of March 31, 2026, under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4).
Kirloskar Oil Engines received a tax demand of ₹5.90 Cr and penalty of ₹0.59 Cr for FY23 from UP GST authorities.
Kirloskar Oil Engines subsidiary KASPL received business commencement approval after ₹9 Cr capital infusion.
Kirloskar Oil Engines announced a new ₹1,400 Cr capex plan for high horsepower engine capacity expansion at its Kagal plant.
Kirloskar Oil Engines received a GST demand order of ₹3.83 Cr including tax, interest and penalty for FY23 from the Deputy Commissioner of State Tax, Pune.

On 7 August 2026 Kirloskar Oil Engines told analysts Q1FY27 standalone revenue rose 16% to ₹1,461 Cr while EBITDA margin fell to 11.2%, and disclosed a first hyperscale data centre order of about 192 MW.
